title: Biological memory preserves salience rather than fidelity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Biological memory preserves salience rather than fidelity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin proposes that memory, across scales from cells to societies, is best understood as preserving salience (what matters for the agent's future) rather than fidelity to the details of the original data.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Using examples from developmental biology, evolution, and synthetic bioengineering, in addition to neuroscience, I propose that a perspective on memory as preserving salience, not fidelity, is applicable to many phenomena on scales from cells to societies.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “Abstract”. Scope: Living systems from cells to societies

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Restricted behavioural versions can be tested with public data, but the all-scale formulation requires substantial interpretation. Existing data cannot adequately represent the full scope or cleanly distinguish salience preservation from ordinary compression and generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For defined memory paradigms, quantify retention of task-relevant predictive value versus retention of stimulus detail after context or embodiment changes. Preferential preservation of future-useful associations across several scales supports the proposal; equal or greater preservation of incidental detail counts against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Salience is agent- and task-dependent.

Selection of examples could make the proposal circular.

No common measure spans cells, organisms and societies.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.45
data existence: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement is a proposed perspective on memory, not a measurement claim. Experiments can show that some memories keep a useful relationship while dropping specifics, and the same outcomes are already described as generalization or retrieval failure. Nothing in existing data would decide that salience is the correct cross-scale account.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A memory assay could score retained detail against retained behavioral relevance, but the claim is that salience-not-fidelity is the best description across cells to societies, and no single pattern of errors would establish that this description is the right one.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Generalization, abstraction, and ordinary forgetting all produce the same loss of detail.

Salience is defined by what later matters to an agent, so the measure presupposes the framing under test.
